title: IDF 188th Brigade and Yahalom Unit Destroy Four Hamas Tunnel Structures in Southern Gaza Including Hostage-Holding Site
detail: The IDF's 188th (Iron Tracks) Armored Brigade, working alongside the Yahalom combat engineering unit, destroyed four underground Hamas tunnel structures in southern Gaza on May 11, 2026 — the first day of renewed IDF operations following the security cabinet's May 10 authorization. The tunnel network, east of the ceasefire Yellow Line, totaled approximately 2.5 miles in length and included infrastructure used to hold Israeli hostages following the October 7, 2023 attack, as well as living quarters belonging to senior Hamas Khan Younis Brigade commanders. Weapons, ammunition, and explosives were found and destroyed inside the tunnels. Simultaneously, the Kfir Infantry Brigade destroyed two additional tunnel routes in central Gaza spanning approximately 1.2 miles, containing rockets, explosives, and hideouts. The IDF said the operations demonstrate that Hamas's tunnel network — estimated at 500+ km at its peak — had been only partially neutralized during the October 2023–October 2025 ground campaign and that Hamas had used the 212-day ceasefire to regroup and reconstruct portions of its underground infrastructure. The operations marked the first significant IDF activity under the formal renewed war authorization.

media.caption: IDF 188th Brigade and Yahalom unit destroy four Hamas tunnel structures in southern Gaza including one that held Israeli hostages — first day of renewed military operations

title: IDF Begins Day 1 of Renewed Gaza Campaign; Evacuation Orders Issued for Eastern Rafah as Operations Resume
detail: Israel launched the first day of its renewed large-scale Gaza military campaign on May 11, 2026 following the security cabinet's formal authorization the previous day. Israeli forces issued evacuation orders for additional areas of eastern Rafah, directing approximately 100,000 civilians to move to designated humanitarian zones ahead of anticipated IDF ground advances. The Southern Command's operational plan — prepared over several weeks — reportedly involves reoccupying Yellow Line buffer zones in southern Gaza and conducting targeted operations against Hamas battalions that had partially reconstituted during the 212-day October 2025 ceasefire. The Board of Peace announced it was halting most field monitoring activities east of the Yellow Line given the resumption of active hostilities. IDF spokespersons confirmed that operations were authorized to expand and that the 'restraint period' was over. Hamas's military wing issued a statement vowing to 'shatter the new invasion as we shattered those before it.' UN humanitarian officials said the Gaza health system — already operating at under 30% capacity with only 17 of 36 hospitals partially functional — could not absorb the trauma caseload of a new major offensive. The UN Secretary-General issued an emergency statement calling for a return to negotiations.

media.caption: Israel launches Day 1 of renewed Gaza military campaign; evacuation orders issued for eastern Rafah as IDF operations resume under security cabinet authorization

title: Gaza Humanitarian System at Breaking Point on Day 943 as Renewed War Begins; Death Toll 72,736+
detail: As Israel's renewed military campaign officially began on Day 943 of the war (May 11, 2026), the cumulative Palestinian death toll stood at 72,736+ confirmed killed and 172,574+ wounded since October 7, 2023. An estimated 14,222 additional bodies remain under rubble, putting the projected total at nearly 87,000. At least 870+ Palestinians had been killed during the 212-day October 2025 ceasefire period alone. The UN WAFA Palestinian news agency updated the ceasefire-period death toll to 870+ killed and 2,433+ wounded as of the day of war resumption. UNRWA reported sheltering over 65,000 displaced Palestinians in 82 emergency shelters, with disease outbreaks — including scabies, chickenpox, and respiratory infections — spreading across all camps. The 2026 UN Humanitarian Flash Appeal ($4.1B required) remained approximately 10% funded. Board of Peace reconstruction funds of $17B+ were frozen pending Hamas disarmament, which Hamas had categorically rejected. With active hostilities resuming, UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs warned of 'an acute and potentially catastrophic deterioration' and called on all parties to ensure the protection of civilians, healthcare facilities, and humanitarian workers. Gaza's European Hospital in Khan Younis issued an emergency statement warning it could not absorb new casualties from a major offensive.

media.caption: Gaza death toll stands at 72,736+ on Day 943 with 870+ killed during the ceasefire period as humanitarian organizations warn of catastrophic deterioration
